usage:
Usage: nscb split <source> [bundle-directory] [--layout canonical|legacy-xc|legacy-ns] [--replace | --skip] [--json | --jsonl]

Split one selected regular file into parts in a bundle. The default layout uses two-digit member names. `legacy-xc` requires byte-recognized uncompressed XCI with eligible structure; `legacy-ns` accepts PFS0 with no NCZ compression established. The source extension is used for naming only and does not establish its family. These checks make no Nintendo identity or authenticity claim. Without a destination, NSCB uses <source-name>.split inside the configured output_dir or Documents/NSCB_output. The bundle contains a <source-name> directory and an adjacent <source-name>.nscb-split.json manifest. The inner directory keeps the full source basename; member names use the basename without its final extension. Resolve accepts the inner directory or one member. The default policy refuses a different existing bundle. An exact qualified match is reported as already up to date; --replace cannot replace a different bundle, and --skip leaves it unchanged. Production part size is fixed at 0xFFFF0000 bytes. The destination filesystem must meet the local APFS qualification. --json emits one job.result document; --jsonl emits ordered job.event records followed by one job.result document. Invocation and planning errors before job admission emit a kind:error document.
created: Split bundle published at {bundle}. Resolve the canonical directory at {canonical}. Manifest: {manifest}.
already_up_to_date: Split bundle already matches the planned source: {bundle}.
skipped: Split left the existing bundle unchanged: {bundle}.
cancelled: Split was cancelled before the receipt commit.
internal_failure: Split ended without an authoritative result.
unknown_error: Split ended in an unrecognized state.
cleanup_warning: Operation-owned recovery data was retained because cleanup could not be proven safe.
